---
title: "The Derivation Primitive"
---

# The Derivation Primitive

At the lowest level, Nix builds packages using the built-in function `derivation`.

A derivation requires three mandatory attributes:
1. `name`: A string identifier.
2. `system`: The target architecture string (`"x86_64-linux"`, `"aarch64-darwin"`).
3. `builder`: The path to the executable executing the build (usually `/bin/sh`).

## Worked examples

Save as `minimal.nix`:

```nix
# minimal.nix
derivation {
  name = "desk-banner";
  system = builtins.currentSystem;
  builder = "/bin/sh";
  args = [
    "-c"
    "echo 'Desk System Online' > $out"
  ];
}
```

Run:

```bash
nix-build minimal.nix
```

Output:

```
these 1 derivations will be built:
  /nix/store/7vqw93...-desk-banner.drv
building '/nix/store/7vqw93...-desk-banner.drv'...
/nix/store/3la841...-desk-banner
```

`$out` is the destination path allocated in `/nix/store`.

## The boring rule

- A derivation is a pure function evaluated into a `.drv` file and realized as a store path.
